Chinese robotics company AheadForm unveiled one of its most lifelike humanoid robot faces at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai. Unlike most humanoid robot demonstrations that focus on walking, running, lifting objects, or performing acrobatic moves, AheadForm showcased highly realistic facial interaction. The robot features natural blinking, eye contact, synchronized speech, subtle head movements, and expressive facial reactions designed to make conversations feel more human. According to the company, its self-supervised AI and high-precision bionic actuation enable coordinated movements of the eyes, mouth, face, and speech, creating a remarkably lifelike communication experience. The result is a humanoid face realistic enough to make people take a second look. #robotics #artificialintelligence #humanoidrobot #waic2026 #technology

Researchers at Keio University and the MIT Media Lab have built a robot you’re actually meant to touch. The soft, helium-filled robot drifts through a room on gentle flapping fins, quiet and free of the loud buzz of a drone.  The idea is to sidestep the “uncanny valley,” the unease that rigid, almost-human robots tend to trigger.  With no face to get wrong and a soft, lightweight body, it communicates through movement alone, the way it hovers, drifts, and leans, and it has no rotors or pinch points to hurt you on contact. In their demos, the team showed it working as an alarm clock that nudges you awake, a study buddy, a reminder to get up and move, even a dance partner.  Their bet is that people will welcome a robot into their personal space, a bit like a pet, as long as the hardware is built to be touched.  If they’re right, the friendliest home robots of the future might not walk or roll. They might simply float. Study: “Floating Companion: Exploring Design Space for Soft Floating Robots in Indoor Environments” DOI: 10.1145/3800645.3813051

videos.caption: I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

Hugging Face is ramping up production of its new open-source robotic ducks after the first 24 hours of preorders blew past what it can ship by year's end.    The Brooklyn-based company launched its $399 Microduck in four colorways shortly after news broke that NVIDIA was buying the AI firm for around $12.9 billion. Hugging Face developed the AI-powered robot in collaboration with Pollen Robotics, its French subsidiary that also made the research-grade humanoid robot, Reachy, and its desktop version for consumers, the Reachy Mini.    The Miniduck is a 25 cm (10 inch) bipedal robot that weighs under 800 grams (1.8 lbs). It has 15 motors in its legs, neck, and head, a beak that can pick up small objects. It moves faster with optional wheels.    The robot perceives its surroundings with a front camera and a small LiDAR depth sensor. A Chinese Rockchip processor powers the duck's onboard artificial intelligence. According to Hugging Face, the Microduck can do basic moves out the box, while users can teach it new tricks in simulation.   Hugging Face says it sold more than $2.5 million of Microducks in the first day of preorders, which equates to more than 6,500 units. #robot #robotics #microduck #robotduck #huggingface
